text: There's actual thunder rolling round out there, and I've got a steel mast and a gull sitting on top of it. AC/DC, Thunderstruck. [to Gerrit] Come down off the aerial. Please.
Everybody ashore is off for the evening. Me, I'm in the wheelhouse with the microphone, as ever. Chef'Special, My Night Off. [dryly] I'll take mine some other year.
Listen to that rain on the wheelhouse roof, then listen to Bonham's drums, and tell me which is heavier. Led Zeppelin, When the Levee Breaks. I've put a bucket under the leak by the chart table.
Showers coming and going over the bay, and light breaking through in between. Keep an eye over the island. The Rolling Stones, She's A Rainbow. [dryly] Gerrit's never once looked up for one.
The wind's got into the rigging and it's making a noise like an out-of-tune choir. Jimi Hendrix, The Wind Cries Mary. Much better at it than my rigging.
Blue sky, hot deck, and the tar between the planks going soft. Queens of the Stone Age, My God Is The Sun. Not a word of argument from Gerrit, who's flat out on his crate.
Clear sky, and I've been turning my chair all day to keep the sun on my face. Xavier Rudd, Follow the Sun. That's as far as a man at anchor can follow it.
Not a cloud, and the light off the water is hard enough to make you squint in the wheelhouse. Eddie Vedder, Hard Sun. Fitting, for once.
Proper sunshine out there. I've got my mug on the deck and my feet on the rail. Two Door Cinema Club. Sun.
Sonnentanz means sun dance, and the sun is dancing on every wave between here and the beach. Klangkarussell. Six minutes. Take your shoes off.
Middle of summer, the deck's too hot to stand on barefoot, and Gerrit's panting with his beak open, which is how gulls complain. Florence + The Machine, Dog Days Are Over. Not yet they're not.
All day and now all of the night, still at the microphone. The Kinks knew the hours a pirate keeps. Lighthouse going round, Opa going steady. All Day And All Of The Night.
